title: Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility
abstract: arXiv:2611.26568v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility $U(x)=-x^{-\gamma}$, $\gamma>0$. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control. A budget inequality and concavity verify optimality over all admissible strategies with nonnegative wealth on every finite horizon, without Novikov's condition. Under the optimal feedback, wealth and consumption admit deterministic upper bounds when the interest rate $r$ is at most the mean-reversion rate $\kappa$. If $r>\kappa$, each exceeds any prescribed level with positive probability at every time after the start. If $r>\sqrt{2+\gamma} \kappa$, there is an explicit critical horizon at and beyond which expected terminal wealth is infinite, while optimal expected utility is finite. translated_title: 负幂效用下配对交易的最优控制
translated_abstract: 我们求解了配对交易模型中一个有限期限的消费与投资问题，其中价差服从Ornstein-Uhlenbeck过程，效用函数为 $U(x)=-x^{-\gamma}$（$\gamma>0$）。通过对Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman方程进行线性化，我们得到了价值函数与最优反馈控制的显式公式。利用一个预算不等式和凹性论证，我们在无需Novikov条件的情形下，验证了在所有于每个有限期限上保持财富非负的容许策略中的最优性。在最优反馈控制下，当利率 $r$ 不超过均值回复速率 $\kappa$ 时，财富与消费具有确定性的上界。若 $r>\kappa$，则在起始之后的每个时刻，财富与消费均以正概率超过任意给定的水平。若 $r>\sqrt{2+\gamma}\kappa$，则存在一个显式的临界期限，在达到或超过该期限时期望终端财富为无穷大，而最优期望效用仍然有限。当临界时刻早于到期日时，期望财富在……
tldr: 本文通过线性化HJB方程，在负幂效用与Ornstein-Uhlenbeck价差的配对交易模型中显式求解了有限期限最优消费投资问题，并刻画了在不同利率与均值回复速率关系下财富与消费的上下界行为，以及期望终端财富发散而最优期望效用保持有限的显式临界期限。
en_tdlr: This paper explicitly solves a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and negative-power utility by linearizing the HJB equation, characterizing deterministic bounds or unbounded growth of wealth and consumption depending on the interest rate versus mean-reversion rate, including an explicit critical horizon beyond which expected terminal wealth becomes infinite while optimal expected utility remains finite.
